name: Upstash QStash
summary: Upstash QStash is a message queue that calls your own API on a schedule or in the background, retrying automatically if the call fails.

free_plan_covers.note: Free plan allows 1,000 messages per day, about 30,000 a month, with 50GB of monthly bandwidth included.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No monthly plan is required after free; pay-as-you-go is $1 per 100,000 messages with no base fee. Fixed plans start at $180/month.

portability.note: QStash just calls your own HTTP endpoint with retries and delivery guarantees, so your handler is normal server code, no workflow syntax to rewrite.

sdk_typescript.note: The @upstash/qstash package is an official TypeScript/JavaScript SDK, alongside a separate Python client.

long_running.note: QStash calls your own endpoint over HTTP, so your host's own request timeout still applies to each delivery.

schedules.note: Cron schedules are built in: add an Upstash-Cron header, or use the schedules API, with a standard cron expression.

setup.step: Create a free Upstash account and open the QStash tab to get your credentials.
Install the SDK with npm install @upstash/qstash.
Copy the token and both signing keys from the QStash dashboard into your environment file.
Publish a message to a server route in your app with the QStash client, and verify each incoming request's signature with the SDK's Receiver.

builder_notes: Verify the QStash signature on every incoming request, with the SDK's Receiver, before trusting the payload.
QStash calls your endpoint over plain HTTP, so keep handlers inside your host's own request timeout, or split long work into multiple scheduled steps.
Use the Upstash-Cron header, or the schedules API, to repeat a job instead of building your own cron runner.
